ev.q: An estimated 6.0% of adults had a current ADHD diagnosis
Demographic distribution among adults with current attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and adults who have never received an attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder diagnosis
reported taking prescription stimulant ADHD medication during the previous 12 months (33.4%)
Almost one half of adults with ADHD (46.0%) reported ever receiving telehealth services for their condition
an estimated 15.5 million U.S. adults (6.0%) had a current ADHD diagnosis based on self-report
When compared with adults who have never received a diagnosis of ADHD, those with current ADHD were more likely to be aged <50 years
The data are cross-sectional and cannot be used to examine trends over time.

methods_quotes.q: responses are weighted and calibrated to the estimates from the second quarter of the 2023 National Health Interview Survey
Variances were computed using the Taylor linearization method.
SAS-callable SUDAAN (version 11.0.3; RTI International) was used to conduct all analyses.
Sample restricted to the 232 adults who reported that they were prescribed medication to treat their ADHD during the previous 12 months.
